sourceSufficiencyAssessment: The supplied brief is itself sufficient primary evidence that its author proposed A–D, compared named assistants and preferred testing C/A. It is not evidence that Observatory has those capabilities, that users will pay, or that integration is cheap. The rebuilt text respects that distinction. Fresh official technical documentation, model card/repositories and actual licence support the retained public factual core; conditional reasoning is an explicitly marked analytical response to those facts. No underlying private document was recovered/read/certified here, and no full-original-research certification is implied.
conditionalReasoningAssessment: Existing Business spending controls, installation dashboards, tool-call history/export/read APIs and community telemetry narrow the old absence premise. They neither prove nor disprove a particular unmet independent distributed data-read audit need. Candidate explicitly asks that question, keeps A/C as proposed tests, leaves B/D as author positions, and avoids demand, engineering-time, revenue or superiority conclusions.
substantiveParityAssessment: All paired titles/bodies and 15 source notes/method notes read. Both languages preserve public-offering versus tested-result qualifiers, per-profile memory/session distinctions, post-training versus base pretraining, code versus model licence, spending versus API billing, and proposal versus validated demand. No material translation mismatch, invented product requirements, user biography, quotes or generic management moral found.
